governing_question: Starting with Arkansas as it actually exists, what is the safest, lawful, fiscally responsible sequence for moving toward Constitutional Capitalism while continuously improving household prosperity and leaving the next generation more capable and wealthy than the one before it?
central_proposition: Constitutional Capitalism begins with stewardship of the state that exists, not destruction of it in pursuit of the state we imagine. Build the bridge before removing the old road—and never claim COUNTABLE replacement capacity that does not yet exist.
organizing_sentence: Pass 3.7 is the roadmap: Arkansas NOW stewardship, full Dependency Rule, Replacement Readiness Test, Build & Prove → Prove & Scale → Structural Transition, Generation 1 success tests, Generation 2 Intergenerational Balance Sheet, Transition Control Board, fiscal transition ledger, and failure/correction architecture—without inventing a fiscal schedule.
hard_boundary: This is a roadmap architecture chapter, not an implementation manual and not a fake multi-year budget. Stage 4 tests numbers. COUNTABLE remains $0 until evidence changes it.

prior_first_pass.role: TR-01–TR-08 first-pass working models integrated into unabridged roadmap. Harvest — deepen, do not reopen as eight new projects.

stewardship_premise.title: We inherit Arkansas
stewardship_premise.principle: Constitutional Capitalism begins with stewardship of the state that exists, not destruction of it in pursuit of the state we imagine.
inherited: Millions of people whose lives cannot become experiments

dependency_rule.title: Dependency Rule — unabridged
dependency_rule.one_line: Build the bridge before removing the old road.
dependency_rule.statement: No existing revenue source, benefit, public service, obligation, or economic institution is removed merely because Constitutional Capitalism proposes a superior replacement. The replacement must first demonstrate the capacity to assume the existing function.
dependency_rule.rule: No existing revenue source, public service, benefit, obligation or institution is removed simply because the future architecture proposes something better. Replacement requires demonstrated capacity.

replacement_readiness_test.title: Replacement Readiness Test
replacement_readiness_test.purpose: The gate between theory and structural change.

tests.question: Does the replacement perform the required function?
Can it operate at necessary scale?
Is it lawful and constitutionally defensible?
Does transition protect households from unacceptable disruption?
Does it preserve competition and functioning economic relationships?
Can Arkansas retreat or correct if implementation fails?

years_1_2.title: Years 1–2 — BUILD & PROVE
years_1_2.label: BUILD & PROVE
years_1_2.objective: Increase the state's ability to know what works.
years_1_2.not: Not every item becomes an immediate legislative proposal.

years_3_5.title: Years 3–5 — PROVE & SCALE
years_3_5.label: PROVE & SCALE
years_3_5.scale_path: Successful local mechanisms → broader pilots → regional/state scale where justified.
years_3_5.public_income_rule: Public-income mechanisms may begin becoming fiscally meaningful only if evidence supports them.
years_3_5.spend_shift: From recurring consumption without capacity creation toward productive investment where appropriate.
years_3_5.not: Don't manufacture a fiscal schedule. Stage 4 tests the numbers first.

years_6_10.title: Years 6–10 — STRUCTURAL TRANSITION
years_6_10.label: STRUCTURAL TRANSITION
years_6_10.when: Only here should we seriously contemplate major replacement of legacy fiscal structures—if and only if replacement capacity exists.
conceptual_order: Legacy tax dependence can potentially decline
years_6_10.correct_sequence: Build replacement → prove replacement → reserve replacement → stress-test replacement → reduce legacy dependence.
years_6_10.wrong_sequence: Abolish tax → hope growth fills hole.
years_6_10.political_importance: This distinction may become one of the most politically important parts of the public book later.

generation_1.title: Generation 1 — success tests
generation_1.insight: A generation isn't merely an election cycle.
generation_1.rule: We don't claim these outcomes. These become the success tests.

intergenerational_balance_sheet.title: Arkansas Intergenerational Balance Sheet

capitals.label: Productive capital
capitals.contents: Infrastructure, enterprises, energy, technology, productive land

intergenerational_balance_sheet.compare: What Generation 1 inherited versus what Generation 1 leaves.
intergenerational_balance_sheet.power: More powerful than asking whether government balanced one annual budget.

intergenerational_capital_rule.title: Intergenerational Capital Rule
intergenerational_capital_rule.rule: A generation should not improve its apparent prosperity by consuming productive, fiscal, natural or institutional capital that the next generation will need.
means: Deferred infrastructure maintenance isn't necessarily fiscal prudence
Depleting natural productive capacity isn't necessarily economic growth
Selling productive public assets to finance current consumption can impoverish the future

transition_control_board.title: Transition Control Board — unabridged
transition_control_board.purpose: Eventually a live administrative instrument, not just a book table.

prior.public_note: Architecture first — no fake public example rows that create confusion.

fiscal_transition_ledger.title: Fiscal transition ledger
fiscal_transition_ledger.rule: Only the final defensible number can support reducing an existing revenue source.
fiscal_transition_ledger.countable: COUNTABLE $0 remains $0 until evidence changes it. That's what prevents the transition chapter from becoming fantasy.

guardrails.label: No speculative replacement
guardrails.rule: COUNTABLE $0 means $0 available for transition planning. Potential revenue cannot replace existing revenue.

guardrails.label: Existing obligations remain real
guardrails.rule: Pensions, debt, contracts, constitutional requirements, federal conditions, and ongoing services do not disappear because the future system differs.

guardrails.label: Pilots earn scale
guardrails.rule: A compelling theory does not earn statewide implementation.

guardrails.label: Transition costs count
guardrails.rule: If a new system requires capital before generating savings or income, that cost belongs in the model.

guardrails.label: Reversibility matters
guardrails.rule: Where practical, early implementation should allow Arkansas to retreat from mechanisms that fail without destabilizing essential services.

political_transition.title: Political transition
questions: How do reforms survive changes in administration?
How are successful systems prevented from becoming patronage machines?
How do future citizens reverse our mistakes?
political_transition.rule: Every transition should eventually have a legal pathway classification. Don't perform every legal analysis now.

human_transition.title: Human transition
human_transition.rule: The system cannot claim prosperity by hiding losses experienced during the transition. Belongs in Household Prosperity accounting.

geographic_transition.title: Geographic transition
geographic_transition.laboratory: Arkansas becomes a laboratory of governed experimentation, while constitutional rights and statewide obligations remain protected.

resilience_before_replacement.title: Resilience before replacement
resilience_before_replacement.rule: A replacement doesn't become REPLACEMENT-READY merely because it works during good economic conditions.

failure_architecture.title: Failure is allowed
failure_architecture.cultural_principle: The system must be better at identifying and terminating failure than conventional government is.
failure_architecture.insight: Failure of a pilot is information. Continuing a failed program because its creators are politically invested is the actual failure.
failure_architecture.anti_excuse: What prevents transition from becoming a permanent excuse? Measurable milestones, transparent gates, public accountability and explicit deadlines/review—not trust in leadership.

architecture_harvest.label: FY2026 GR distributed — inherited fiscal baseline join
architecture_harvest.note: Join Arkansas NOW / Money Engine — not a transition revenue claim

gaps: Legal pathway classifications per reform OPEN → Stage 4
Intergenerational Balance Sheet series values UNKNOWN by design

integration_spine.title: From Arkansas NOW to Generation 2
integration_spine.while: COUNTABLE stays $0; Stage 4 stress-tests before legacy dependence disappears.

counterarguments.claim: Why should voters wait years for change?
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Stewardship premise + Dependency Rule. Immediate abolition without Replacement-Ready capacity is not courage—it is household disruption. Years 1–2 still deliver measurement, transparency, pilots and KEEP/REFORM/PHASE OUT decisions.

counterarguments.strong_form: Local success always fails at scale.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Evidence classes include INCONCLUSIVE. Scale is earned, not assumed. Resilience-before-replacement and reversibility tests exist precisely because pilots are imperfect predictors.

counterarguments.strong_form: Transition Control Board is capture by delay.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Failure architecture requires STOP/PHASE OUT/ELIMINATE. Capture Loop breakers (3.5) + Comprehensible Government + measurable milestones prevent permanent excuse. Anti-excuse rule is explicit.

counterarguments.strong_form: Human and fiscal transition costs dominate any gain.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Human transition costs count; fiscal ledger includes Transition Costs and Reserves. If net benefit fails Replacement Readiness, HOLD—not force.

counterarguments.claim: Future legislatures will raid accumulated public assets.
counterarguments.strong_form: Any reserve is a future slush fund.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Ring-fence, waterfall, COUNTABLE discipline, Capture Loop breakers, sunset/review (3.4–3.5). Stage 4 adversarial raid scenarios required before REPLACEMENT-READY on fiscal structures.

counterarguments.claim: Government cannot accurately identify failed programs.
counterarguments.strong_form: Every program finds a constituency and never dies.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Cultural principle: better at terminating failure than conventional government. Explicit STOP/REFORM/PHASE OUT/ELIMINATE paths + public measurement. Trust is not the mechanism—gates are.
Geographic transition allows start modes by need and capacity while constitutional rights and statewide obligations remain protected (3.5 subsidiarity).

counterarguments.claim: Building reserves unnecessarily delays household tax relief.
counterarguments.strong_form: Every reserved dollar should have been a tax cut yesterday.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Wrong sequence is abolish→hope. Correct sequence is build→prove→reserve→stress-test→reduce. Premature relief that reopens fiscal holes fails household security.

counterarguments.strong_form: Ten-year roadmaps die at the next election.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Political transition questions require statute/constitutional/local/voter pathway classifications; sunsets; reversibility. Survive by institutions and gates, not personality.

counterarguments.claim: A 10–30 year framework cannot survive democratic politics.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Intergenerational Balance Sheet + Capital Rule make long-horizon accounting a democratic artifact citizens can demand—not an elite plan above politics. Generation 1 success tests are public.

counterarguments.claim: Intergenerational accounting imposes today's preferences on future citizens.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Rule constrains consumption of capital future citizens need—not their policy choices. Reversibility and citizen sovereignty (3.5) preserve their agency.

counterarguments.claim: What prevents transition from becoming a permanent excuse for never delivering?
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Measurable milestones, transparent Replacement Readiness gates, public Accountability Loop, explicit review deadlines, and failure exits—not trust in leadership. Permanent excuse fails the anti-excuse rule.
